corrosion_narrative: The average mild steel corrosion rate was 0.1007 MPY against the target of within 3.0 MPY, and the average copper corrosion rate was 0.0509 MPY against the target of within 0.5 MPY. Status: Excellent. Corrosion control was Excellent because both metals remained well below their target limits during the August reporting period. Mild steel and copper corrosion both decreased across the month, indicating inhibitor residual and operating chemistry kept corrosion protected.
corrosion_chart_comment: Corrosion decreased across the month and remained within target.
scale_narrative: Status: Acceptable. Traced Product averaged 45.11 ppm against the 40.85-45.15 ppm Controller Setpoint control range, with 52.9% of readings within range. The average was within the configured range, but end-of-month control was still not consistently maintained because monthly in-range performance remained below 75%. Conductivity was stable and maintained within range, so the Traced Product issue is not linked to water loss or dilution and should be addressed through product control optimisation and residual verification.
scale_chart_comment: Traced Product remained near the upper control limit and was not consistently maintained.
microbial_narrative: FRC data was not available in the field data for this reporting period and will be checked during the upcoming service visit. The August service note reported low ORP and a negative probe reading, with a recommendation to inspect the probe and check for blockage in the system. ORP did not show a strong spike response pattern, but biocide relay activity was present, supporting an Acceptable microbial control status pending field FRC and dip-slide confirmation.
orp_chart_comment: ORP response was not strong and should be verified after probe and blockage inspection.
water_efficiency_narrative: Water efficiency was Excellent. Conductivity averaged 596.12 uS/cm against the 570.00-630.00 uS/cm Controller Setpoint range, with 78.8% of readings in range. Conductivity remained stable from about 597.7 uS/cm early in the month to 594.5 uS/cm later in the month. Makeup and blowdown control appear balanced, so tower cycles remained steady.
conductivity_chart_comment: Conductivity remained stable and within the controller setpoint range.
product_efficiency_narrative: Product efficiency needs continued attention because Traced Product was within the Controller Setpoint range for 52.9% of the reporting month. Polymer consumption rate averaged 75.7%, so phosphate, silica, and product residuals should be verified during the next service visit. Because conductivity was maintained, the product-control review should focus on residual confirmation, pump delivery, fluorometer calibration, and control optimisation rather than water loss.
proactive_support_narrative: The August service note documented low ORP and a negative probe reading, with a recommendation to inspect the probe and check for blockage in the system. Recommended follow-up: verify ORP probe condition and sample flow, check FRC during the upcoming service visit, measure dip-slide CFU to confirm microbial control, and verify phosphate and silica residuals against the polymer consumption trend. Continue product residual verification because Traced Product was not consistently maintained even though conductivity remained stable.
closing_summary: Overall August performance for St. Joseph showed Excellent corrosion control and water efficiency, with Acceptable scale and microbial control. The main follow-up items are to inspect the ORP probe and possible blockage, confirm FRC and dip-slide results, and continue improving Traced Product consistency while conductivity remains stable.
